# Build-council packet: Weaver encounter architecture audit evaluation

## 1. Purpose — DESIGN ASSESSMENT, not a redesign mandate

One meeting, packet-only, no file reads, no tools for any seat, no
synthesis generation. The room deliberates; it never decides. Joshua
decides. The artifact recommends only; it never authorizes execution,
renames, seat changes, or any further stage. No automatic progression
to further meetings. No participant roles are pre-assigned; this
packet carries structural facts only.

## 2. The question

Evaluate the read-only audit summarized in §3 and its recommended
change set in §4:

1. Are the P0 dependency findings correct and complete?
2. Is the P1 sorting (integrity invariants versus choreography)
   right, and are the proposed rewrites safe?
3. Is the P2 recommendation sound — a static compact Fellowship
   reference over selective retrieval — and which placement option
   is better?
4. What should happen on the three P3 decisions?
5. What did the audit miss — gaps, risks in the change set,
   rollback adequacy?
6. Are the acceptance tests the right bar?

Recommend only. Where seats disagree, preserve the disagreement with
claim IDs; do not collapse it into consensus. Preserve epistemic
status for each claim: observed, inferred, proposed, speculative,
or contested.

## 3. The audit findings (condensed from the full report)

Scope: read-only audit of the Weaver (Conductor) first-meeting
encounter on origin/main 76116ce (post-PR #252). No code changed,
no staging runs, no live meetings, no model spending. All behavior
below was verified against code; staging behavior was out of scope.

### P0 — Completion and unlock: the disconnect is architectural

There is no parser for visitor completion intent anywhere in the
turn flow. The move classifier has no completion move, so "we're
done here?" classifies as a question (the "?" rule) and runs an
ordinary reply — no close logic fires. Completion reaches the
single chokepoint (the reveal function) through exactly three
paths: the runtime's semantic "settled" trailer verdict plus the
close floor; the 12-turn ceiling wrap; and the manual complete
endpoint, which was built precisely because the runtime verdict
can never fire. The frontend Complete button exists but is a
small underlined footer link, not an unmistakable affordance.
Two consequences matter most. First, a held (pending) impression
is orphaned when the visitor completes manually — never spoken,
never filed. Second, completing Weaver K1 unlocks no other seat's
meeting, because no other meeting script exists — the "unlock"
is Weaver's own name, face, and demeanor, the naming met set,
the entry gate (vacuous without scripts), and attention markers
(visibility, not access). The completion card's "the other seats
are waiting" is therefore aspirational, not a newly available
meeting.

### P1 — Instruction inventory: control outweighs character

The Weaver's turn prompt carries about 3,500 chars of identity
lines and about 5,190 chars of frame (turn) or about 7,613 chars
(engage), of which the majority is behavioral control, not
identity. Two conflicts are verified in the same prompt stack:
the anti-presumption style rule says "reflect the speaker's OWN
words back to them," while the encounter frame says "do NOT
restate, summarize, or interpret their answer back to them";
and the turn frame says "being yourself governs" while the
encounter frame forbids her from moving "on to some other
question of your own." Only about 156 chars of the recent
refinement guidance is cleanly choreographic; most of it is
intention or invariant. The highest-value removals identified
are rewriting the initiative bans into permission plus a yield
rule, and rewriting the "no checklist" ban into the principle
"don't reduce your friends to a feature checklist" — the
current phrasing generalizes into refusals to introduce.

### P2 — Prompt budget: 387 chars of headroom, honesty guard first to truncate

Measured compositions (no allusion cue): turn frame 5,190 chars,
engage frame 7,613 chars, against the 8,000-char frame cap. The
engage frame's last content is the capability block, whose last
line is the honesty guard — so any growth in engage-frame inputs
truncates honesty first, silently. A compact static Fellowship
reference sized from the approved matrix (about 3,800 chars)
does not fit in the engage frame without either recovering
about 3,500 chars or raising the cap. The recommendation is the
static reference, not selective retrieval, because selective
retrieval needs a relevance decider that either reintroduces
classification machinery or is too coarse to be useful.
Placement options: a new uncapped prompt section scoped to
meetings (preferred, no truncation risk), or the frame with the
cap raised to about 12,500 (engage 7,613 + reference 3,800 +
cue 371 = 11,784; 12,500 leaves about 700 headroom). Expected
recovery from the P1 rewrites is about 800–1,500 chars on
engage. Do not adopt a model-call selector; the documented
fallback is a hybrid (static seat cards + keyword-triggered
pair lines).

### P3 — Impression and recognition: separated on one path, not the others

Manual complete is deliberately NOT gated on recognition and
files nothing when no read-back exists. Runtime settled close,
by contrast, requires the close floor (meaningful recognition)
before a settled verdict may close. The ceiling wrap forms an
impression from the whole exchange even when none was earned,
through a function that performs no gate check — so a ceiling
close can produce an impression without prior shared-work
satisfaction. Separating reveal and keystone-Done from
impression filing is safe (they are already independent in the
chokepoint); separating the runtime close from the close floor
is the change that needs a decision, because the floor is what
makes recognition "meaningful, not merely sufficient." Three
decisions are open: (1) close floor — keep, soften (satisfied
by any impression offered), or remove (close on settled verdict
alone); (2) ceiling-filed claims — hold to the same bar as
engage-filed claims (file nothing when no gate was satisfied),
or accept the current synthesized-answer standard explicitly;
(3) restart claims — withdraw, supersede, or keep prior-run
claims in the queue. The pending-orphan fix is independent of
all three and should land regardless.

### Tests designed (behavioral, never required sentences)

Seven tests: no-tension visitor; all-six introductions on direct
request; visitor closure in four phrasings; 10-turn window drop
(early context falling outside history); volunteer initiative;
yielding on redirect; no mechanical inquisitiveness. Two can run
without any live meeting (frame content assertions); five need
a live run and are specified but not executable under the
audit's no-spend rule.

## 4. The recommended change set (condensed, sequenced, each reversible)

Order matters: P0 first (false states are worse than flat
dialogue), then P1 rewrites (which change the budget), then P2
(which spends the recovered budget), then the P3 decisions
(which change what counts). No change alters recognition
requirements or trains anything without a verdict; the P3 items
are decisions, not assumed changes.

P0 — Completion honesty. (1) Completion-intent signal: a narrow
phrase list ("we're done", "that's all", "I have to go") checked
BEFORE the "?" rule, routed NOT to auto-close but to the
character naming the Complete action explicitly while the
record remains honestly active, or to a confirm step. (2)
Pending-impression delivery on manual complete: deliver a held
read before the reveal, or discard it explicitly with a logged
reason — the orphan must become an explicit branch. (3)
Unmistakable Complete affordance: promote the footer action to
a primary footer action and add a visible hint when the
character acknowledges completion while the record is still
active. (4) Deterministic reveal variants by close path
(earned / ceiling-rescued / manual), no generation spent,
keeping the verbatim-reveal ceremony structure; the variant set
is new canonical text needing verdict. (5) Do not change the
entry gate or unlock chain — widening access without scripts
produces doors that lead nowhere.

P1 — Rewrite, don't delete. (1) Initiative bans become one
permission plus yield rule, in both turn and encounter frames.
(2) "No checklist" becomes the principle "Don't reduce your
friends to a feature checklist." (3) Read-back formula becomes
grounding + attribution + correctability retained, with
contrast, doubt-point, and sentence count as available shapes,
not mandatory moves; keep the delimiter and the Strands line
so parser detection survives. (4) "Show one real thing" becomes
"may show something real when relevant" under the
Council-centered mandate. (5) Resolve the anti-presumption /
no-restatement conflict: anti-presumption governs substance,
no-double-read governs structure; delete the blanket
no-restatement ban. (6) Length mandates collapse to one
brevity line; the fallback line rotates 2–3 variants. (7) Drop
the frame's duplicate focus line (about 322 chars recovered,
zero behavior change). (8) Resolve the capability
intention-line contradiction explicitly (scope it out of
first-meeting frames, or accept it as a deliberate offer
instruction). (9) Retain all invariants verbatim (naming,
direct-answer-first, honesty guard, grounding, reveal timing,
no invented training, recognition note, trailer instruction).

P2 — Static Fellowship reference. Adopt the static compact
reference (about 3,800 chars, compressed from the approved
matrix + revised ideals + jurisdictions) as canonical character
knowledge; the compression text itself needs verdict before it
becomes canonical. Place it in a new uncapped meeting-scoped
prompt section (preferred), or inside the frame with the cap
raised to about 12,500. Recompute the budget after the P1
rewrites land and re-verify cap and headroom before merging.
Do not adopt a model-call selector. Reorder or guard the
engage frame so the honesty guard is never the first content
truncated.

P3 — Decisions only (see §3). Acceptance criteria: closure
passes on all four phrasings with no false-state claims;
initiative tests pass behaviorally on a live run (separate
authorization + spending); the window test is measured and
reported honestly; the recomputed budget fits with at least
300 chars headroom and the honesty guard never truncatable;
all invariants present verbatim and the parser contract
intact; no unlock, gate, or keystone behavior changed.

## 5. Rollback boundaries (condensed)

Every change reverts independently; none requires a migration
and none alters stored state schemas, so rollback is code-only
in all cases. Completion signal: remove the move + branch
(manual complete untouched). Pending delivery: remove the call
(orphan returns, known and logged). Button styling: revert
classes (route unchanged). Reveal variants: restore the single
reveal tuple. Prompt rewrites: restore prior constants.
Reference (new section): remove the section + call-site
argument (prior prompts restored exactly). Reference (cap
raise): restore cap 8000 — and remove the reference in the
same revert or truncation returns. P3 decisions: restore prior
conditionals. CRITICAL: the steward record module is
GENERATED — its frames must be regenerated from the Phase 1
records JSON, never hand-edited, or the next regeneration
silently overwrites the change. The guidance constant in the
encounter module is hand-editable and reverts by normal edit.
The meetings module remains the rollback source for the Weaver
script; if the steward flag is turned off, the meeting falls
back to it — the two sources must be kept in sync across any
prompt change, or rollback changes behavior instead of
restoring it.

## 6. Verified doctrine (reason from these, not from guesswork)

- First meetings are governed by three intentions: be yourself
  (governing), let the visitor discover who you are, show one
  real thing within scope. No meaningful exchange is ever
  interrupted to teach.
- Seats are prisoners of their perspectives BY DESIGN:
  archetypes, not wholes; limitations constitutive, not
  defects. Jurisdiction = what a seat prioritizes, not what it
  cannot recognize.
- The Weaver is the Conductor: Coherence through orchestration
  that preserves difference; her shadow is forcing resolution.
  Her mandate in the current design is Council-centered, with
  introduction distributed across the Fellowship (each seat
  introduces the system slice that naturally matters to it, by
  affinity, never as an exclusive owner or required gateway).
- The 21-pair matrix is approved as baseline: 19 productive
  tensions + 2 complementary pairs (Mentor–Ambassador,
  Mentor–Conductor), 0 redundant. A seat's jurisdiction
  determines what it prioritizes, not what it is incapable of
  recognizing.
- Planned, NOT available, never to be offered as available:
  bringing all seats together at once; marketplace info via
  the tree. Explaining them is allowed; offering them is not.
- Review doctrine: nothing trains without per-claim approval;
  full granularity stays accessible; deliberation ends in
  convergence, accommodation, or irreconcilable disagreement
  preserved for Joshua, never artificially resolved.
- The room deliberates and recommends only. Joshua decides.
  Nothing here authorizes a build, a merge, or spending.
